summary: Live console rollup windows lag and hourly usage undercount during high ingest bursts for BrightAudit org
description: Issue summary: BrightAudit support reported that the Console live metrics and hourly usage cards are lagging by 30-90 minutes and showing undercounted tokens during a large customer batch ingest that began 2026-03-10 09:12 UTC. Impact: Reporting and billing-sensitive dashboards are inaccurate for the customer; alerts tied to hourly thresholds did not fire. Environment: Production (us-east) on dedicated stack for BrightAudit. Observed: Live rollup windows stall, new events appear in raw logs but do not show up in hourly rollups; rollup service consumer lag is high and retry rate increased. Expected: Sub-minute propagation from raw events -> rollup aggregation -> console UI for live/near-real-time cards.
impact: BrightAudit internal dashboards and billing report show 15-40% lower usage for the affected hour range; customer escalated citing potential invoice disputes. Several internal SLOs for console freshness are breached for this customer during the window.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Trigger a sustained high-volume batch of inference events from a dedicated customer (approx 1200 req/s sustained over 10 minutes).
2) Observe raw event ingestion in Kinesis/consumer logs (ingest-pipeline).
3) Check rollup-service consumer group lag and rollup queue depth.
4) Open Console -> Usage -> Hourly cards and Live Metrics; note delay between raw events and aggregated numbers.
logs: ingest-pipeline consumer lag metrics: consumer_group=rollup-consumer, lag=~120000 msgs, 2026-03-10T09:18:12Z
rollup-service error samples: RetryableKafkaError: fetch timed out (x127 retries), 2026-03-10T09:19:07Z
console backend trace id: trace:ae3f2c1b - missing hourly-aggregation for window 2026-03-10T09:00Z
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: sudden spike produced consumer backlog and triggered retry backoff which paused rollup application for certain partition keys (likely due to hot-shard behavior).

Checked Kafka metrics: one partition had sustained fetch failures; broker reported brief GC spikes around 09:16Z. Correlated with a managed maintenance event on the broker cluster? (pending cloud-provider confirmation).
Observed that compacted backfill job (daily-rollups) was running concurrently and held DB write locks on the aggregation table for ~4 minutes, which magnified client retry behavior.
Temporary mitigation test: increased rollup-service consumer parallelism for BrightAudit tenant (from 4 -> 8) in staging-like environment and re-ran a synthetic burst; consumer lag recovered to <30s.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:35 - Support (Anita Rao): Customer reported missing tokens in hourly card; escalated to SRE. Added BrightAudit to incident call #support-incidents.

2026-03-10 09:50 - SRE (Diego Morales): Dug into consumer lag and Kafka broker GC spikes. Opening ticket against rollup-service and reaching out to infra for broker maintenance logs. @infra please confirm any planned maintenance affecting us-east brokers.
2026-03-10 10:12 - Infra (Lina Chen): Confirmed brief broker GC spike due to JVM heap compaction during 09:15-09:18Z triggered by monitoring agent update. We'll roll back the agent and monitor.

2026-03-10 10:45 - Support (Anita Rao): Customer accepted temporary mitigation of increasing consumer parallelism while engineering investigates root cause. Requested ETA on full fix to avoid repeated billing discrepancies.

2026-03-11 08:22 - Eng (Diego Morales): Implemented short-term backfill job to recompute affected hourly windows for BrightAudit and kicked off job; monitoring rollups show numbers aligning now. Preparing PR to add locking/backoff improvements to rollup-service.
root_cause: Concurrent broker GC spike combined with a long-running daily compaction/backfill process caused elevated consumer fetch timeouts. Rollup-service retry/backoff logic and DB write lock behavior amplified the delay for specific partition keys (tenant hotspot), resulting in delayed hourly rollups and undercounted console usage during the window.
resolution: Workaround: increased rollup-service consumer parallelism for affected tenant and ran a targeted backfill to recompute the missed hourly aggregates. Long-term fix: PR submitted to improve rollup-service's backoff handling and to add adaptive consumer-parallelism per-tenant; infra to revert monitoring agent that triggered GC spike and add broker-side alerting for GC pause >500ms. Customer notified of backfill and provided corrected hourly numbers.
follow_up_actions: 1) Merge and deploy rollup-service PR to add tenant-aware parallelism and safer DB lock patterns (PR #452).
2) Update runbook 'Live Rollups' to include steps for increasing consumer parallelism and triggering targeted backfills.
3) Add broker GC pause alerting to infra playbook and coordinate with cloud provider to avoid agent-induced pauses.
4) Review billing reconciliation process with Finance for affected invoices from BrightAudit window and offer credit if needed.
5) Add a console alert for 'consumer_lag > 60s for 5m' scoped to dedicated tenants.
